items.root_cause: The scaler data block mixes two bases and nothing declares or checks which one gpu is on: grams and pkg_g are drained (the engine moved them there), gpu is still the ingredient row GROSS grams per feed unit (28.3495 g/oz on a 15.25 oz can whose contents drain to 298 g). Any formula that pairs grams with pkg_g is right; any that pairs grams with gpu is a category error. build-card2:134 checks the first pairing (ceil(grams/pkg_g) == buy_n) and never the second (pkg_g/gpu == the physical can), so the block ships with a fallback package of 10.5 oz for a 15.25 oz can and nothing throws. The error is invisible while densities.can equals buy_pkg_g (both bases coincide) and becomes reachable the moment an item gets a real drained yield: beans since the feed repoint, corn at 09:16 today, pineapple at 17:24. It reaches the reader only through the feed packageBasisUnits path, which every store cell of every canned bid takes. The same count rule exists in three places on three bases (engine pkg_g; widget/compute-v2 gpu x feed; planner gross buy_pkg_g), and a fourth divergence rides along: the widget and its PowerShell mirror round with ceil(x - 1e-9) while the engine, the render lib, build-card2 check and the planner round with ceil(x - 0.02), which splits the count on the engine own package whenever frac(x) is in (0, 0.02] - 12 same-package lines today, 3 drained lines after the basis fix alone. This is [[two-copies-of-a-rule]] and [[repair-stops-at-source-of-truth]]: corn01 fixed the engine basis and stopped at the renderer. audit-twin-drift could not see it because it compares TEXT and the copies are in two languages with the same text and different inputs.

root_fix.what: ONE count rule, ONE basis, ONE tolerance, and a guard that compares COUNTS. (1) gpu_eff via Get-ScalerGpu everywhere (surface_fix). (2) Align the widget and its mirror to the engine tolerance: tpl2:316 `Math.ceil(required/packageBasis-1e-9)` -> `-0.02`, package-cost-lib.ps1:52 `- 1e-9` -> `- 0.02`; the planner :272 already uses 0.02. (3) Declare the tolerance as a twin in ops\twin-rules.json (captured constant 0.02 across cost-recipes.ps1:301, cost-render-lib.ps1:104, build-card2.ps1:134, compute-v2:195, tpl2:316, package-cost-lib.ps1:52, meal-plan-builder-template.html:272); audit-twin-drift is a text comparer so it pins the constant, not the basis - say so in the why. (4) The basis is pinned by OUTCOME: build-card2 throws when the block fallback package is not the physical package (surface_fix); compute-v2 -CrossCheck additionally compares, per line, the block own count at the authored basis `ceil((grams/gpu)/(pkg_g/gpu) - 0.02)` with costed buy_n and exits 2 on any disagreement; wave-preaudit gets check widget-count-basis (below) so a card whose widget count disagrees with its cost line is refused before the wave auditor ever sees it.

That script REGENERATES THE FROZEN INPUTS FROM LIVE DATA and refuses without -Reseed, which is the one thing a frozen fixture must never do. Used golden-test.ps1 -Rebaseline instead, which re-runs the engine over the SAME pinned inputs and rewrites only expected\. Verified the accepted diff is the new field and nothing else: pkg_gross_g added on 202 lines (differing from pkg_g on 4), zero other field changes across all 14 fixture recipes. golden-test 13 passed 0 failed after. D2 cost-recipes PLACEMENT: the plan keys pkg_gross_g off $DRAINED.ContainsKey. Set it from $pg.g inside the buy-package branch instead. Identical value on every line today (the DRAINED net IS $pg.g), but it cannot misfire if a drained item ever becomes bulk, where $pkgG is the pantry container and the plan's form would have divided by the wrong package. D3 THE PLAN'S -CrossCheck COUNT COMPARISON IS A TAUTOLOGY: ceil((grams/gpu)/(pkg_g/gpu) - 0.02) against buy_n cancels the gpu, and returns 4 for street corn's block both before and after the fix. Its own self-test caught it on the first run. Shipped it as a STALENESS check (a card on disk against a costed row that has since moved) and added the check that does fire: the block's authored fallback package against the physical package, which reported 122 of 7843 lines on the pre-fix cards and 0 after. Both self-tests now pin the tautology so nobody re-adds the dead half as the live one. D4 EMITTED gpu: build-card2 reads the SPEC's gpu (street corn 28.350) while the artifact used ingredients.json's (28.3495), so the shipped block carries 19.5563 where ship_sequence step 5 and held_cards say 19.5559. 1.8e-5 relative; no count moves at any serving count 2..42 on either lane. bounced_findings: NEW CLASS, found while implementing corn04 and NOT fixed here (a different mechanism, and its fix is a JS change this plan's do_not_touch forbids). THE DEFECT: build-card2 signals "this line has no purchase" by emitting pkg_g 0 on a covered_by line, relying on the widget's pkgBasis() returning 0. But pkgBasis() reads the feed's packageBasisUnits FIRST and only falls back to pkg_g/gpu, and every store cell of every priced commodity carries a packageBasisUnits - so pkg_g 0 is never consulted and costAt() prices the line at the store's package. build-card2's own comment beside that emit asserts the opposite ("the widget already guards its buy maths on pkg_g>0 && gpu>0"), and that assertion is false on exactly the path every priced commodity takes. This is the same shape as corn04 (a block field the JS only partially honours, reachable only through the feed packageBasisUnits path) but it is a different bug with a different fix. THE MEASUREMENT: db\costed.json holds 2 covered_by lines, on 2 recipes, 1 of them live. no-boil-chicken-pasta-casserole-with-artichokes-and-peas :: Lemon Zest (covered by Fresh Lemon Juice, LIVE): block pkg_g 0, gpu 6, grams 5; the widget charges $0.85 for one lemon at Baker's on BOTH lanes, while the static cost line and compute-v2 both charge nothing. street-corn-chicken-rice-bowls :: Lime Zest (covered by Fresh Lime Juice, not yet live): $2.07 for three limes at Baker's on both lanes. PRE-EXISTING, PROVEN: the pre-rebuild card, saved before anything was rebuilt today, charged the identical $2.07, so this is not a regression from corn04 - it has been live since the covered_by suppression shipped on 2026-09-01 (queue 2026-09-01-b5b8e0) and nothing ran -CrossCheck between then and now. READER IMPACT TODAY: one live card overstates its widget basket by $0.85 a batch ($0.06 a serving at 14), and the receipt contradicts the cost line two inches above it, which is the exact contradiction covered_by was written to remove. WHY IT IS VISIBLE NOW: compute-v2 -CrossCheck exits 2 on it (2 total disagreements, both this class, after 0 count disagreements). The guard is correct and was left failing closed; -CrossCheck is not in the daily chain (check-ad-cycles :742 runs compute-v2 without it), so nothing in the chain is broken by leaving it red. NOT FIXED HERE because the fix belongs in costAt/pkgBasis (treat a line with pkg_g 0 as no purchase) and this plan's do_not_touch forbids changing costAt beyond the one tolerance constant, and because zeroing the block's gpu instead would make the widget mark the WHOLE receipt unavailable (required 0 -> costAt null -> totalAt incomplete), which is worse. Needs its own round.
